full_judgment:
Md Imman AIi J: These three civil appeals, by leave, are directed against the judgment and order dated 5-8-2003 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition Nos.1518, 1519 and 1520 of 2003 making the Rules Nisi absolute. These appeals are heard together, and they are dealt with by this single judgment. 

 3. Section 26(1) of the VAT Act, 1991 provides, infer alia, that a VAT Officer authorised for the purpose by the Commissioner or Divisional Officer may enter the premises upon serving notice to inspect the goods, raw materials and the accounts etc. relating to business for the purpose of audit, provided that such Commissioner or Divisional Officer upon stating reasons may authorise in writing an officer not below the rank of Superintendent to enter and inspect without prior notice and such an officer will submit a report of such inspection to the Commissioner or Divisional Officer within 48 hours. Section 48 of the VAT Act provides that the National Board of Revenue or an authorised Commissioner of VAT having jurisdiction or someone not below the rank of an Assistant Commissioner VAT, may authorise any VAT Officer to search any premises and seize goods therefrom. The aforesaid sections 26 and 48 do not authorise writ-respondent Nos.1 and 2 to enter, inspect, search any premises or offices for VAT purposes or to seize goods and documents therefrom. Writ-respondent Nos.1 and 2 could exercise powers only in relation to customs. National Board of Revenue by its memo dated 19-10-1998 clearly stated that writ-respondent Nos.1 and 2 have no authority to enter, inspect or search any premises under the VAT Act or rules made thereunder and that their jurisdiction is limited to customs inspection, investigation and audit. Section 40 of the VAT Act provides that for adjudication of cases punishable with fine the Divisional Officer is the person empowered and authorized in that behalf. Section 37 of the VAT Act provides that the offences mentioned in section 37(1) and 37(2) are punishable with fine. Section 42 provides for appeal to the Commissioner from the order of the Divisional Officer passed in an adjudication under section 40. Writ-respondent No.2 having no authority under the VAT Act to act in any manner relating to VAT or to inspect the office and factory of the writ-petitioner located at Dhaka and Barisal seized various documents therefrom on 6-2-2002 and thereafter submitted a report on 28-3-2002 (Annexure-A) making various allegations against the writ-petitioner and suggested issuance of the notice of demand under section 55(1) of the VAT Act. Acting on the aforesaid report writ-respondent No.3 by its memo, dated 24-2-2002 issued a notice to show cause upon the writ-petitioner asking it as to why an amount of Taka 58,15,27,043.66 shall not be realised from the writ-petitioner as VAT under section 55(1) and why the writ-petitioner should not be fined under sections 37(1) and (2). The writ-petitioner by its letter dated 20-6-2002 replied to the said show cause notice denying the allegations and explaining the full facts and circumstances. It is submitted that the aforesaid search and seizure conducted by writ-respondent Nos.1 and 2 and the report dated 28.3-2002 submitted by writ-respondent No.2 are absolutely arbitrary, mala fide, for collateral purpose and without lawfully authority, inasmuch as writ-respondent Nos.1 and 2 have no authority under the VAT Act to conduct such inspection, search and seizure. It is pointed out by the writ petitioners that section 26 of the VAT Act or a Divisional Officer VAT has the right to so enter inspect, verify and examine stocks, records, documents etc. and nobody else. Writ-respondent No.2 not being such an officer the said inspection, search and seizure are ultra vires the provision of the VAT Act. Furthermore, the aforesaid search and seizure was not conducted on the order of the Board or the Commissioner or duly authorised VAT Officer in exercise of powers under section 48 and, as such, the search and seizure made by writ-respondent No.2 is in violation of the provisions of section 48 and is therefore arbitrary, main fide, for collateral purpose and without lawful authority. The adjudication initiated and show cause notice dated 24-4-2002 alleging violation of section 37(1) and (2) are illegal, inasmuch as section 37 provides for fine for the offence mentioned therein. Section 40 provides that in cases of offence punishable by fine the adjudication will have to be done by the Divisional Officer. Section 42 of the VAT Act further provides that an appeal against an order of adjudication by a Divisional Officer shall lie to the Commissioner. In the circumstances the impugned memo dated 24-2-2002 initiating an adjudication process by writ-respondent No.3 is without lawful authority and of no legal effect inasmuch as the Commissioner being the appellate authority ought not to have initiated the proceeding which could only have been initiated by the Divisional Officer. In the circumstances the proceeding in question is beyond jurisdiction of the provision of VAT Act. Besides the Commissioner being the appellate authority could not initiate the proceeding under the law. 

 4. Writ respondents contested the Rule Nisi and denied the allegations made in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that respondent. Nos.1 and 2 had been authorised by the National Board of Revenue under section 48 read with section 24 of the VAT ACT and hence the search and seizure was lawful. Therefore, the report and consequent action taken by the respondents are in accordance with law. 

 5. After hearing the parties, by the impugned judgment and order, the High Court Division made the Rules Nisi absolute. Against which the writ-respondents filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1446-1448 of 2003 before this Division and leave was granted to consider the following submissions of the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners: 

 "I. That as per provision of section 21 of the VAT Act 1991 read with rule 6 of VAT Rules, 1991 the Commissioner or any officer of VAT can perform any duty or exercise power assigned to his subordinates. As per provision of section 42(1)(Ka) the Commissioner (Appeal) is the appellate authority against an adjudication order passed by an Assistant Commissioner. As per section 42(I)(Kha) of VAT Act, 1991 the appellate tribunal is the appellate authority against an adjudication order passed by the Commissioner or equivalent officer. 

 IV. That the inspection, search and seizure effected by the officers of the team comprising VAT Officers, Inspection and Audit Officers and in presence of local Assistant Commissioner and Superintendent, VAT has got every legal authority as per provision of section 48 read with section 24 of the VAT Act, 1991." 

 6. Mr Samarendra Nath Biswas, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. In addition he submitted that the National Board of Revenue is empowered to delegate its power of search of any premises to a Commissioner, VAT, DG, Inspection Directorate of Customs Excise and VAT or an officer of VAT not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner and the Customs authority exercise powers under section 24 of the VAT Act (under instructions from the competent authority). He submitted that the Chairman National Board of Revenue instructed the office of the Director General, Customs Intelligence and Investigation to find out the evasion of Value Added Tax made by the appellant maintaining strict secrecy and appellant No.2 acted accordingly on 6-2-2002 in accordance with the provision of section 24 of the VAT Act, 1991 comprising officers of Customs, Excise and VAT South Commissionerate, Dhaka, North Commissionerate, Dhaka and Director General, Inspection Directorate (who are VAT Officers) including officers of Customs Intelligence and Investigation Department. At the time of inspection, the Assistant Commissioner and Superintendent of VAT of the jurisdiction were also present. Subsequently, the action was also approved by the Chairman, National Board of Revenue within two working days. The search and seizure was conducted under section 48 read with section 24 of the VAT Act, 1991. On the basis of the specific direction of the Chairman, National Board of Revenue appellant Nos. 1 and 2 investigated into the matter with the officers of different VAT Commissionerate, Inspection Directorate and in presence of Assistant Commissioner and Superintendent of VAT of the jurisdiction. Furthermore, the report dated 28-3-2002 prepared by appellant No.2 submitted to the National Board of Revenue as sought by them. National Board of Revenue forwarded the report on 7-4-2002 to the Commissioner VAT, Khulna for taking necessary and lawful action tinder the signature of Member (VAT) which established the legal authority exercise by appellant No.2 in this matter. He submitted that as per provision of section 21 of the VAT Act 1991 read with rule 6 of VAT rules, 1991 Commissioner or any officer of VAT can perform any duty or exercise power of his subordinates. As per provision of section 42 (1)(Ka) the Commissioner (Appeal) is the appellate authority against an adjudication order passed by an Assistant Commissioner. As per section 42(1) (Kha) of VAT Act, 1991 the appellate tribunal is the appellate authority against an adjudication order passed by the Commissioner or equivalent. He submitted that the Chairman, National Board of Revenue directed appellant No.2 to investigate into the matter, and the activities done by appellant No.2 has got every legal authority. He submitted that the show cause notice was issued by appellant No.3 and the respondent did not deny the charge of evasion of Taka 58,15,27,034.66 as framed by appellant No.2 prepared on the basis of documents seized from the respondent's premises. The respondent tried to misinterpret the provisions of VAT Act and Rules and the respondent's reply was irrelevant and unjustified on material points. In this case the notice of demand and show cause dated 22-4-2002 (wrongly mentioned as dated 02-2-2002 in the writ petition) served by appellant No.3 initiating adjudication process was made with lawful authority under section 21 of the VAT Act. The respondent company should have lodged an appeal before the Appellate Tribunal as per section 42(1)(Kha) of the VAT Act. Moreover, the respondent was served with notice for four times by appellant No.3 to show cause personally or through his lawyer but the respondent prayed for time again and again for submitting reply and after submitting reply the respondent also prayed for shifting the date of hearing on flimsy grounds. The respondent filed the writ petition before the High Court Division superseding the normal departmental procedures. He submitted that the inspection, search and seizure conducted by the officers of the team comprising of VAT Officers, Inspection and Audit Officers and in presence of local Assistant Commissioner and Superintendent, VAT who has got every legal authority as per provision of section 48 read with section 24 of the VAT Act, 1991. He submitted that it is proved and found from the documents that the respondent has evaded a huge amount of Government Revenue amounting of Taka 58,15,27,043.66. He lastly submitted that appellant Nos.1 and 2 having been authorised by the National Board of Revenue under section 48 read with section 24 of the VAT Act, 1991 entered into the office and factory premises of the respondent and searched and seized various documents of the respondent therefrom and submitted reports and appellant No.3 in pursuance thereto legally issued the notice calling upon the respondent to show cause as to why the respondent should not pay the amount demanded/adjudicated against respondent for resorting to illegal means to defraud the government by non-payment or short payment of VAT. 

 7. Mr AM Aminuddin, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondents in all the appeals submitted that writ-respondent Nos.1-2 having had no such authority either under section 26 or section 48 of the Act carried out the impugned search and seizure of the documents of the writ-petitioner through Al-haj Taibur Rahman, Superintendent of Customs, Excise and VAT in Dhaka after entering into the premises and offices of the writ-petitioner at both the places, thus the impugned search and seizure of the documents of the writ-petitioner by the writ-respondent Nos.1-2 are without jurisdiction. He submitted that the impugned notice of demand with show cause to the writ-petitioner are also illegal and without jurisdiction, inasmuch as the same were issued by writ-respondent No.3, Commissioner of VAT, instead of by a Divisional Officer as it involved imposition of fine only and not confiscation of any goods or commodity as contemplated under section 40 of the Act, conversely, since the impugned notice of demand with show cause involved imposition of fine only without confiscation of goods, the said notice was to be issued by the Divisional Officers and not by the Commissioner of VAT as contemplated under section 40 of the Act. In essence, the learned Advocate restated the submissions which were placed before the High Court Division. He submitted in fine that neither writ-respondent Nos.1-2 nor said Al-haj Md Taibur Rahman were authorised under section 26 or section 48 of the Act to enter the premises for inspection, search or seizure of books, documents and papers of the writ-petitioner for the purpose mentioned therein and except the aforesaid provisions of law under sections 26 and 48 there is no other law to take care of any case involving non-payment, short payment or fraudulent withholding of payment of VAT by any person or business concerned. 

 8. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates appearing for the parties concerned and perused the impugned judgment of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record. 

 9. We find from the judgment of the High Court Division that upon scrutiny of section 26(1) and 48 of the VAT Act, 1991 it found that respondent No.2 and Al-haj Taibur Rahman did not have the authority to make any search and seizure. It was further observed that section 48 of the Act does not empower the NBR to authorise respondent Nos. 1 and 2 to make such search and seizure as they are not VAT officers. Hence, the report dated 28-3-2002 emanating from such illegal search and seizure prepared and issued by respondent No.2 are illegal, without jurisdiction and coram non judice. 

 10. The learned Deputy Attorney-General submitted before us, as was submitted before the High Court Division that the National Board of Revenue is empowered to delegate its power to search any premises to a Commissioner, VAT, Director General of Inspection Directorate of Customs Excise and VAT or an officer of VAT not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner and the Customs authority exercised powers under section 24 of the VAT Act 1991 and the search and seizure was therefore legal, particularly since the Assistant Commissioner and Superintendent of VAT were also present. He emphasised that the search and seizure was conducted under section 48 read with section 24 of the Act, and on the basis of specific direction of the Chairman, NBR writ-respondent Nos.1 and 2 investigated into the matter. 

 11. We find from the report dated 28-3-2002 that during the search and seizure Aminur Rahman (writ respondent No.2), Joint Director, Customs Intelligence and Investigation headed a team which raided M/s Opsonin Chemical Industry Ltd, Bogura Road, Barishal. Another team headed by one Taibur Rahman, Superintendent, Customs Excise and VAT Inspection Directorate, Dhaka, raided the head office of the same company in Dhaka. According to the report the search and seizure was conducted under the authority of section 26 and 48 of the Act. Section 24 of the Act provides that assistance may be taken by the VAT officer (মূল্য সংযোজন কর কর্মকর্তা) from the Police, Bangladesh Rifles (now Border Guard Bangladesh), Bangladesh Coast Guard and Bangladesh Ansar. Hence, we find that the power exercised in conducting the search and seizure was in fact under section 26 read with section 48 of the Act and that section 24 is in that circumstance only an auxiliary provision for the purpose of taking assistance from the forces mentioned therein. 

 12. Section 26(1) of the Act permits any VAT officer authorised by the Commissioner or Divisional Officer to conduct search and seizure upon serving notice. The proviso to the said section permits the Commissioner or Divisional Officer, upon giving reasons, to authorize any VAT Officer not below the rank of Superintendent to carry out search and seizure without giving notice. In the facts of the instant case we note that writ respondent No.2, who conducted the search and seizure was a Joint Director of Customs Intelligence and Investigation and not a VAT Officer. We further note that Md Taibur Rahman, who headed another team and conducted search and seizure of the appellant company, was a Superintendent of Customs Excise and VAT. 

 13. Clearly section 48 of the Act provides that NBR can direct search and seizure to be conducted by a VAT Officer not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner to carry out search and seizure. 

 14. We are of the view that the High Court Division was correct in holding that neither respondent No.2 nor the said Al-haj Md Taibur Rahman were authorised under section 26 or section 48 of the Act to enter the premises of the respondent company for the purpose of search and seizure.
